svg.data-optics-qsfp-dd: 800GE QSFP-DD OpenZR+/ZR/2xLR4/2xFR4/DR8+/DR8/SR8; 400GE QSFP-DD OpenZR+/ZR/ER4/LR4/FR4/SR8/DR4/DR4+/PLR4; 200GE QSFP56 SR4/FR4; 100GE QSFP28 ZR4/ER4/SR4/LR4 (datasheet Compatible Transceivers). Per-port optical power is budgeted 16 W on ports 0-31 and 23 W on ports 32-63 (HIG Figure 9 note)
svg.data-optics-sfp28: 1G/10G/25G SFP28 up to 40 km (HIG Port Overview table, ports 64-65; the datasheet's Compatible Transceivers list covers only the QSFP-DD field)
svg.data-timing: Stratum 3E OCXO; SyncE; IEEE 1588v2 (default, G.8265.1, G.8275.1, G.8275.2); T-TC, T-BC/OC, T-GM
svg.data-console: RJ45 RS-232 and micro-USB, both labelled IOIO, 115200 8N1 (micro-USB needs the Silicon Labs CP210x driver)
svg.data-timing-inputs: 1x 1PPS in/out SMB and 1x 10MHz in/out SMB, both Premium-build only
svg.data-emc: FCC Part 15 Subpart B Class A; ICES-003 Class A; EN 55032 Class A; EN 300 386; EN 55035; VCCI CISPR 32 Class A
svg.data-nebs: NEBS statements only (Common Bonding Network suitability, GR-1089 intra-building port restriction, external SPD required on AC) - the HIG prints the compliance statements without claiming a NEBS level, and none is claimed here

rect.data-members: pps mhz mgmt usb console console-usb

g.data-description: HIG ID row - Off (no power), Solid Blue (reserved - the vendor's own word, so the state is carried without a meaning), Blinking Blue (enabled beacon feature)
g.title: led-id

g.data-description: 1PPS input/output, 50 ohm SMB, Premium build only; HIG Connecting the 1PPS Interface - cable no longer than 3 m, BNC via the accessory converter cable
g.title: pps

g.data-description: 10MHz input/output, 50 ohm SMB, Premium build only; HIG Connecting the 10MHz Interface - cable no longer than 3 m
g.title: mhz

g.data-description: HIG SYNC row - Off (timing/clock synchronization disabled or free-run), Solid Green (timing core synchronized to PTP packet (Phase) or an external timing source (Phase) and frequency locked), Blinking Green (synchronized to PTP packet (Frequency) or an external timing source (Frequency)), Solid Amber (acquiring state or holdover), Blinking Amber (synchronization fail, or acquiring/holdover time out)
g.title: led-sync

g.data-description: HIG SYS row - Off (no power), Solid Green (Host CPU/BMC boot complete), Solid Amber (power is up but Host CPU/BMC boot failed)
g.title: led-sys

g.data-description: HIG FAN row - Off (fans are not initialized), Solid Green (all FAN modules are working normal), Blinking Amber (FAN fail: one or more FAN module(s) need service)
g.title: led-fan

g.data-description: HIG PS0 row - Off (no power), Solid Green (PSU0 is working normal), Solid Amber (PSU0 fail, PSU0 need service)
g.title: led-ps0

g.data-description: HIG PS1 row - Off (no power), Solid Green (PSU1 is working normal), Solid Amber (PSU1 fail, PSU1 need service)
g.title: led-ps1

g.data-description: the OOB management jack (HIG Figure 4 callout 'RJ45 OOB'); its two integrated lamps - left green for 1G link and activity, right amber for 10M/100M, per the HIG Management port LED table - are drawn as led-a/led-b of this jack
g.title: mgmt

g.data-description: USB 3.0 Type-A; the HIG calls it a maintenance port and prints the usbreset and 5V-restart commands beside it
g.title: usb

g.data-description: the second console port, labelled IOIO like the RJ45 one; needs the Silicon Labs CP210x USB-to-UART driver (HIG Initial System Setup)
g.title: console-usb

g.data-description: the two 10/25G SFP28 management uplinks, stacked in one ganged shell left of the QSFP-DD field; the vendor numbers them 64 and 65, continuing the QSFP-DD range rather than restarting, which is what rel-pos carries
g.title: port-64

g.data-description: the two 10/25G SFP28 management uplinks, stacked in one ganged shell left of the QSFP-DD field; the vendor numbers them 64 and 65, continuing the QSFP-DD range rather than restarting, which is what rel-pos carries
g.title: port-65

g.data-description: one lamp per traffic port - 32 on the strip above the upper QSFP-DD band, 32 on the strip below the lower one, and a pair under the SFP28 legend
g.title: led-port-64

g.data-description: one lamp per traffic port - 32 on the strip above the upper QSFP-DD band, 32 on the strip below the lower one, and a pair under the SFP28 legend
g.title: led-port-65
